title: Functions: parameters, multiple returns and named returns

videos.script: Lesson 11 wrote small functions like addFour without stopping to look at them. This lesson stops and looks. {{params}} First, parameters. Go writes the name first and the type second, the other way round from C and Java. Type it the old way and the compiler reads your code as something else entirely. There are no default values either, and no two functions may share a name. {{multi}} Then results. A Go function can return two values, and most of the standard library does: a result, and an error saying whether it worked. You will see what the compiler says when you ignore one, and how to throw one away on purpose. {{named}} Last, results with names. They make the documentation clearer, and they allow a bare return. One mistake with them the compiler refuses outright. {{defer}} By the end you can read any signature in go doc and say what goes in and what comes out.
